newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares see-saw, led by dollar, Wall Street.
newsitem.headline: German shares see-saw, led by dollar, Wall Street.

text.p: German shares see-sawed on Friday, pushed repeatedly to record highs on the back of the firm dollar and short-lived euphoria after soft U.S. data, but momentum faded at the end of the day.

The IBIS DAX index, which tracks all-day screen-based trade in 30 blue chip shares and had risen strongly Thursday, ended the day down 7.69 points at 3,249.17, more than 20 points below its record intraday high of 3,271.91.
That was little changed from the close of the floor trade session, which the DAX ended up 18.70 points at 3,248.18, another record closing high.
The DAX was led by the nose by external factors during the day, leaving dealers uncertain as to its next likely move.
"We've had 13 days of unbroken gains," said a Munich dealer. "Everyone is waiting for the correction and it will happen -- the big mystery is the timing."
A weaker-than-expected start on Wall Street undermined confidence in the afternoon, despite soft U.S. inflation data, showing producer prices dropped 0.3 percent in January.
"The basic message is -- moderate growth and low inflation. It couldn't be better," said a German dealer of the data.

Banks were the biggest movers of the day, rising after Morgan Stanley upgraded its outlook for their stocks while Moody's Investor Service said it had placed Dresdner Bank's AAA credit rating under review.
Shrugging off the news, Dresdner shares climbed 50 pfennigs to 53.90 marks in bourse trade, as it said it did not expect any refinancing problems even if Moody's went ahead with the downgrade.

Metallgesellschaft rose 1.32 marks to 34.15 marks after Thursday's late news that it had decided not to take on a 49.99 percent stake in industrial holding company AGIV -- a move which the market feared would have diluted its profits.

However utility Viag declined six marks to 703 after posting a rise in 1996 profit that was broadly in line with expectations, but prompted some shift of interest to rivals in the sector whose earnings position is still unclear.

Looking ahead, Wall Street and the dollar were expected to remain the key focus but attention will also be directed at German data due, including the Ifo business climate index, M3 money supply data, and the regular Bundesbank meeting.
Next week's triple-witching options expiry could also spark some volatility on prices as the week progresses.
